Speech is still being transcribed with the screen off.
A button that floats beside your own keyboard. Hold it in any app, speak, and what you said is typed where your cursor is.
Doodoo records only while you are holding the button. The clip is deleted the moment it comes back as text, and goes nowhere but Groq.

Doodoo uses Android\'s Accessibility service to show its button beside your keyboard and to type what you dictate into the field you are in. It checks only which field has the cursor. It does not read or store what you type or what is on screen, and sends none of it anywhere.

The button below opens Doodoo\'s own page. Turn on the Doodoo switch and leave \"Doodoo shortcut\" off: the shortcut only adds a second floating button you don\'t need. If the switch is greyed out, go to Apps → Doodoo → ⋮ → Allow restricted settings, then come back.
Recording from other apps is allowed
Doodoo transcribes with your own Groq key: no account, no subscription. The free tier covers normal dictation.

Doodoo uses this to place its button on the edge of your screen and to type what you dictate into the field you are in. It looks at where the cursor is and nothing else, keeps no record of what you type, and sends audio only to Groq with your own key.
